answer.rationale: Contract expiration provides critical leverage for renegotiation. Memory_c4 shows benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, indicating current refusal to reopen the *existing* contract may not extend to new terms. With 14 days to expiration and assembly at 94% utilization with no buffer, immediate negotiation is the only path that can potentially meet the 18% cost mandate without introducing supply disruption risk (memory_c1 confirms renewal preserves integration stability). Switching or adding sources risk disruption under current capacity constraints; deferral risks immediate supply gap.
